questions.question: Identify the most efficient method for evaluating the integral.

moves.name: u-Substitution (u = x^2)
moves.professor: The derivative of the exponent is sitting right there. One clean substitution, and the enemy is wide open.

moves.name: Integration by Parts
moves.professor: IBP against a non-linear exponent? You'll trap yourself in a loop. That's a swing at nothing.

moves.name: Partial Fractions
moves.professor: This isn't a rational function. Wrong weapon for this battlefield.

moves.name: Trigonometric Substitution
moves.professor: No square root of a quadratic in sight. You're bringing a siege tower to a duel.

questions.question: Select the critical first move for this integral.

moves.name: u-Substitution (u = 1 + cos x)
moves.professor: Derivative of the denominator is -sin x. With a sign adjustment, the substitution strikes true. Direct hit.

moves.name: Multiply by (1 - cos x)/(1 - cos x) and simplify
moves.professor: This road eventually reaches the target, but through heavy terrain. You'll waste time and risk a misstep.

moves.name: Integration by Parts (u = sin x, dv = 1/(1+cos x) dx)
moves.professor: Putting sin x as u leaves you with a messier integral. This attack rebounds straight at you.

moves.name: Trigonometric Substitution (x = 2 arctan t)
moves.professor: Weierstrass substitution here is like using a catapult to kill a fly. Overkill, and you'll likely miss the clean strike.

questions.question: Which approach slays this integral most cleanly?

moves.name: u-Substitution (u = x^2 + 1)
moves.professor: Numerator is exactly half the derivative of the denominator. One stroke, and the integral falls.

moves.name: Trigonometric Substitution (x = tan θ)
moves.professor: This will work, turning the fight into a trig dance. Slower, but you'll survive.

moves.name: Partial Fractions
moves.professor: Denominator is irreducible over reals. Trying to decompose this is hitting an armored shield with a stick.

moves.name: Integration by Parts
moves.professor: No product of different function types. IBP has no purchase here; your blade glances off.

questions.question: Determine the fastest route to the antiderivative.

moves.name: u-Substitution (u = ln x)
moves.professor: Derivative of ln x is 1/x, right there. One simple substitution, enemy down.

moves.name: Recognize as (1/2)(ln x)^2 derivative
moves.professor: True sniper sight. You can just write the answer, but the substitution path is the reliable blade.

moves.name: Integration by Parts (u = ln x, dv = 1/x dx)
moves.professor: That sets up a recursive nightmare. You'll chase your own tail until you collapse.

moves.name: Trigonometric Substitution
moves.professor: There's no quadratic root here. This weapon is completely wrong—you'll wound yourself.

questions.question: What is the decisive move for this integral?

moves.name: u-Substitution (u = sin x)
moves.professor: cos x dx becomes du instantly. The exponential stays simple. Clean execution.

moves.name: Integration by Parts
moves.professor: Exponential with trig inside resists IBP. You'll get nowhere and take a counter-hit.

moves.name: Trigonometric identity to rewrite integrand
moves.professor: You could try to expand, but it leads to a thorny path. Not a fatal error, but a needless detour.

moves.name: Partial Fractions
moves.professor: This is not a rational function. You're brandishing the wrong weapon entirely.

questions.question: Choose the most effective opening attack.

moves.name: u-Substitution (u = x^3)
moves.professor: x^2 dx is one-third of du. Perfectly aligned. One swift strike ends it.

moves.name: Integration by Parts
moves.professor: Exponent is cubic, not linear. IBP will bog you down in a swamp of terms.

moves.name: Tabular Integration by Parts without substitution
moves.professor: Without fixing the exponent first, tabular is a recipe for disaster. You'll break formation.

moves.name: Trigonometric Substitution
moves.professor: Where's the square root? Swinging a heavy mace at shadows.

questions.question: Which method dispatches this integral with the least effort?

moves.name: Partial Fractions
moves.professor: Denominator factors into (x-3)(x+3). Partial fractions slice it into two logarithms. Efficient kill.

moves.name: Trigonometric Substitution (x = 3 sec θ)
moves.professor: Possible, but you'll navigate a thicket of trig and end up with the same result. Time-consuming.

moves.name: u-Substitution (u = x^2 - 9)
moves.professor: du = 2x dx, but there's no x in the numerator. Your sword meets empty air.

moves.name: Integration by Parts
moves.professor: 1/(x^2-9) isn't a product. IBP has no grip; you'll stumble immediately.

questions.question: Identify the critical technique for this trigonometric integral.

moves.name: Save one sin, convert sin^2 to 1 - cos^2, u = cos x
moves.professor: An odd power of sine is a gift. Peel one off and the rest collapses into a polynomial in cos x. Perfect.

moves.name: Use power-reduction formulas repeatedly
moves.professor: This grindstone still sharpens the blade, but it will take many turns. You'll win, but slowly.

moves.name: Trigonometric Substitution
moves.professor: No root of a^2 - x^2 here. You're mistaking a trig battle for a substitution fight. Painful miss.

moves.name: Integration by Parts
moves.professor: Powers of trig functions resist IBP unless paired with exponentials. You'll just inflame the integral.

questions.question: What is the fastest way to evaluate this integral?

moves.name: u-Substitution (u = x^2 - 4)
moves.professor: Numerator x is half the derivative of the inside. The square root yields to a simple power. One hit.

moves.name: Trigonometric Substitution (x = 2 sec θ)
moves.professor: This path also leads to victory, but you'll fight through extra trig simplification. Solid, but not optimal.

moves.name: Partial Fractions
moves.professor: A radical in the denominator laughs at partial fractions. Wrong battlefield tactic.

moves.name: Integration by Parts
moves.professor: IBP here won't simplify the root. You'll lose footing immediately.

questions.question: Choose the decisive move for this integral.

moves.name: u-Substitution (u = tan x)
moves.professor: The derivative of tan x is sec^2 x, perfectly placed. One blow, integral collapses.

moves.name: Rewrite as cot x sec^2 x and integrate
moves.professor: That just complicates the field. You're maneuvering into rough terrain unnecessarily.

moves.name: Integration by Parts
moves.professor: Sec and tan as a product? IBP here is a trap. You'll get entangled.

moves.name: Trigonometric Substitution
moves.professor: No square root of sum/difference of squares. This weapon is useless here.

questions.question: Identify the best opening to evaluate this integral.

moves.name: Substitute u = x^2, then Integration by Parts
moves.professor: First, tame the inside with u-sub, then IBP on u cos u. Two clean strikes, done.

moves.name: Integration by Parts directly (u = x^3, dv = cos(x^2) dx)
moves.professor: dv = cos(x^2) dx is not integrable in elementary terms. You've walked right into an ambush.

moves.name: Trigonometric Substitution
moves.professor: The battle is about the cosine of a square, not a square root. Wrong intel.

moves.name: Tabular Integration by Parts on original
moves.professor: Tabular needs a clean polynomial times exponential/trig of linear argument. Here it shatters on the x^2 inside cos.

questions.question: Select the method that breaks this integral open.

moves.name: Integration by Parts (u = arctan x, dv = dx)
moves.professor: A lone inverse trig function is a classic IBP target. Set u as the function and dv=dx. Flawless.

moves.name: Substitution x = tan u
moves.professor: You'll end up with ∫ u sec^2 u du, which still needs IBP. A detour, not a shortcut.

moves.name: Recognize as derivative of something simple
moves.professor: No elementary function has arctan x as its simple derivative. Wishful thinking won't slay this foe.

moves.name: Partial Fractions
moves.professor: arctan x is not a rational function. You're swinging the wrong weapon entirely.

questions.question: What is the critical step for integrating this?

moves.name: Rewrite as cos x / sin x, u = sin x
moves.professor: Cotangent is just cosine over sine. The derivative of sine sits on top. A textbook kill.

moves.name: Use formula ln|sin x| directly
moves.professor: Recognizing the standard result works, but knowing why keeps you sharp for variants.

moves.name: Integration by Parts
moves.professor: IBP on cot x alone gives nothing but a headache. You'll waste a turn.

moves.name: Partial Fractions
moves.professor: This isn't a rational function in x. Wrong tactical decision.

questions.question: Which initial approach leads to a quick victory?

moves.name: Complete the square, then use arctan formula
moves.professor: The denominator becomes (x+1)^2 + 4. An arctan awaits. Swift and decisive.

moves.name: Partial Fractions over complex numbers
moves.professor: Technically possible, but you're dragging the fight into the complex plane needlessly. Impractical.

moves.name: u-Substitution (u = x^2 + 2x + 5)
moves.professor: du = 2x+2, not a constant. Your sword hits air. Try again.

moves.name: Integration by Parts
moves.professor: No product form here. IBP is a dead end.

questions.question: Choose the most efficient weapon for this fight.

moves.name: Integration by Parts (u = x, dv = e^{-x} dx)
moves.professor: Polynomial times exponential. IBP with the polynomial as u is a clean, classic kill.

moves.name: Tabular Integration by Parts
moves.professor: Tabular is just IBP in formation. Works perfectly, same result.

moves.name: u-Substitution (u = -x) alone
moves.professor: Substitution alone leaves an x that becomes -u, giving ∫ -u e^u du, which still needs IBP. You only half-drew your blade.

moves.name: Trigonometric Substitution
moves.professor: Exponential with negative x? No root. This weapon is from a different war.

questions.question: Which method breaks the stalemate cleanly?

moves.name: Trigonometric Substitution (x = sec θ)
moves.professor: The form sqrt(x^2 - 1) calls for secant. The whole mess collapses to ∫ dθ. Quick victory.

moves.name: u-Substitution (u = x^2 - 1)
moves.professor: You need an x in the numerator, but it's in the denominator. The substitution misfires.

moves.name: Integration by Parts
moves.professor: IBP with a radical inverse? It'll only grow thorns. Stay away.

moves.name: Partial Fractions
moves.professor: The root blocks any rational decomposition. You can't breach that wall.

questions.question: What is the correct battle plan for this integral?

moves.name: Integration by Parts twice and solve for the integral
moves.professor: This is the classic loop tactic. IBP returns the same integral, then you isolate it. Like a boomerang that hits the enemy.

moves.name: Use Euler's formula to rewrite cosine
moves.professor: Complex exponentials turn this into a power fight. Advanced technique, but it works.

moves.name: u-Substitution (u = ln x)
moves.professor: You get ∫ cos u * e^u du, which is back to the same form. No progress, and you've left your flank open.

moves.name: Trigonometric Substitution
moves.professor: There's no quadratic root hiding here. Your weapon has no target.

questions.question: Seek the most efficient path to the antiderivative.

moves.name: Polynomial division: x^2/(1+x^2) = 1 - 1/(1+x^2)
moves.professor: The integrand is an improper rational function. Divide and conquer—then a simple arctan remains.

moves.name: Trigonometric Substitution (x = tan θ)
moves.professor: This also works, but the division method is quicker. You'll still win, just with more sweat.

moves.name: Partial Fractions
moves.professor: Denominator is irreducible quadratic. Partial fractions can't decompose it further. You're hitting an iron wall.

moves.name: Integration by Parts
moves.professor: No product here. IBP is a ghost swing.

questions.question: Identify the opening gambit that leads to swift resolution.

moves.name: u-Substitution (u = x^2 - 2x + 5)
moves.professor: The derivative of the denominator is 2x-2, exactly double the numerator. One substitution finishes it.

moves.name: Complete the square and use trigonometric substitution
moves.professor: Possible, but why march through a swamp when a straight road is available? Waste of energy.

moves.name: Partial Fractions
moves.professor: Denominator doesn't factor over reals. This attack shatters on impact.

moves.name: Integration by Parts
moves.professor: Rational function not in product form. IBP is a dead draw.

questions.question: What is the sharpest move to crack this integral?

moves.name: Simplify using cos^2 x - 1 = -sin^2 x, then integrate csc x
moves.professor: A keen eye spots the Pythagorean trap. Simplify to -csc x and the integral is standard. Decisive strike.

moves.name: Substitute u = cos x, then use partial fractions
moves.professor: This path works, leading to ∫ du/(u^2 - 1) and partial fractions. A bit longer, but you'll get there.

moves.name: Integration by Parts
moves.professor: You'll bury yourself in recursive trig integrals. A tactical blunder.

moves.name: Trigonometric Substitution
moves.professor: No root of a^2 - x^2. This weapon is for a different monster.
